section_summary: This section covers political developments in Japan from January through August 1934, centering on the terminal decline of the Saito Cabinet and the formation of the succeeding Okada Cabinet. Key crises undermining Premier Saito included the resignation of War Minister Sadao Araki, bribery allegations surrounding Education Minister Ichiro Hatoyama and Commerce Minister Kumakichi Nakajima, General Senjuro Hayashi's temporary resignation over a family scandal, and the devastating Kuroda bribery scandal in the Finance Ministry. Following the Saito Cabinet's en bloc resignation in July 1934, Admiral Keisuke Okada formed a moderate compromise cabinet retaining key ministers and balancing bureaucratic, military, and party elements.

subfiles.about: Reporting hypotheses regarding General Sadao Araki's resignation as Minister of War and his replacement by General Senjuro Hayashi.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew analyzes conflicting explanations for the resignation of War Minister General Sadao Araki. While officially attributed to illness, observers point to Araki's isolation within the cabinet, military budget friction, and resentment among younger army officers. The appointment of General Senjuro Hayashi is seen as a possible victory for moderate elements favoring political non-involvement by the army.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 15 from Tokyo (Resignation of War Minister Araki)

subfiles.about: Analyzing political and historical factors behind the forced resignation of Minister of Commerce Kumakichi Nakajima.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum examines the attacks against Baron Nakajima in the Diet over his past writings praising Ashikaga Takauji. It notes that the invocation of imperial dignity was merely a cloak for political maneuvering and underlying practical conflicts. Nakajima's replacement, Joji Matsumoto, is noted as unfamiliar to the division.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum on Resignation of Baron Nakajima

subfiles.about: Reporting the resignation of Commerce Minister Baron Nakajima and the appointment of Joji Matsumoto.
subfiles.summary: Baron Nakajima resigned as Minister of Commerce and Industry and has been succeeded by Joji Matsumoto. The change is not expected to alter general cabinet policy, with the resignation attributed to criticism regarding his close ties to private steel works during the industry's consolidation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 24 from Tokyo (Resignation of Baron Nakajima)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note indexing a telegram on the resignation of the Minister of Commerce.
subfiles.summary: A State Department document file note cross-referencing Tokyo Telegram regarding the resignation of the Japanese Minister of Commerce, filed under 102.81 Tokyo/227.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/224

subfiles.about: Transmitting a commercial and economic summary covering Japanese foreign trade, gold purchase policy, and the Commerce portfolio change.
subfiles.summary: A report from the Commercial Attaché in Tokyo transmitted by Ambassador Grew reviews business conditions, trade growth in raw silk and textiles, and wholesale price index figures. It reports Diet discussions on a gold-buying bill allowing the Bank of Japan to purchase domestic gold at market price, alongside mention of the Commerce Minister's resignation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 148 from Tokyo (Commercial Attaché Report)

subfiles.about: Reviewing the political background and bribery allegations leading to the resignation of Education Minister Ichiro Hatoyama.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum outlines charges that Education Minister Ichiro Hatoyama accepted a Yen 50,000 fee for using his influence to obtain imperial decorations. It discusses Hatoyama's ties to Seiyukai President Suzuki and assesses potential factional fractures within the Seiyukai and their impact on the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum on Resignation of Ichiro Hatoyama

subfiles.about: Reporting the resignation of Education Minister Hatoyama and Premier Saito's assumption of the portfolio.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Minister of Education Hatoyama resigned on March 3, and Prime Minister Saito has assumed the education portfolio concurrently.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 37 from Tokyo (Resignation of Hatoyama)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 683 concerning attacks on the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A State Department document file note cross-referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 683 (filed under 894.00/506) regarding the Saito Cabinet and political attacks against it.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/226

subfiles.about: Fragment of an intelligence or attaché report regarding Japanese cabinet regulations on minister incapacity.
subfiles.summary: A short, heavily degraded report extract citing Article 9 of the Japanese cabinet regulations concerning the discharge of ministerial duties when a minister is incapacitated. Distribution notes indicate submission by military attaché staff.
subfiles.title: Attaché Report Fragment on Cabinet Regulations

subfiles.about: Reporting the resignation of War Minister General Senjuro Hayashi following his brother's bribery conviction.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that General Hayashi tendered his resignation as Minister of War following the bribery conviction and sentencing of his brother. Premier Saito intends to request the Emperor to decline the resignation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 66 from Tokyo (Resignation of War Minister Hayashi)

subfiles.about: Reporting that General Hayashi withdrew his resignation as Minister of War following imperial and military consultations.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that after conferring with Prince Kan'in and General Mazaki, General Hayashi withdrew his resignation and agreed to remain as Minister of War.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 68 from Tokyo (Hayashi Withdraws Resignation)

subfiles.about: Internal State Department cover note praising Tokyo Despatch No. 753 drafted by Crocker.
subfiles.summary: A brief departmental memorandum highlighting Embassy Tokyo's Despatch No. 753 regarding General Hayashi's resignation and withdrawal, remarking that it was drafted by Edward Crocker.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Division Memorandum on Despatch No. 753
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Detailed diplomatic report on General Hayashi's resignation, family dishonor in the Tokyo Gas scandal, and political aftermath.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides a comprehensive account of General Hayashi's resignation following the ten-month bribery sentence imposed on his brother, Yukichi Shiragami, in connection with the 1929 Tokyo Gas scandal. Adhering to Japanese custom regarding family honor, Hayashi insisted on retiring until Prince Kan'in and General Mazaki persuaded him to reconsider in the national interest. Grew notes that anti-cabinet army factions attempted to exploit the crisis, but Hayashi's popularity ultimately strengthened the Saito administration.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 753 from Tokyo (Resignation of General Hayashi, Minister of War)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a report on Hayashi's succession to Araki as War Minister.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing a report on the succession of General Araki by General Hayashi as War Minister of Japan, filed under 894.00 P.R./74.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/231

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a periodic report discussing the Saito Cabinet's survival despite growing weakness.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 745 (894.00 P.R./76) analyzing why the Saito Cabinet remains in power despite scandals and weakness.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/232

subfiles.about: Extract from Periodic Report No. 76 analyzing internal Japanese political affairs and cabinet stability.
subfiles.summary: This section of Embassy Tokyo's periodic report reviews the Saito Cabinet's ability to survive the 65th Diet session despite attacks over Hatoyama's bribery charges and Kokumin Domei opposition. It details Takahashi's resistance to impeachment over Yokohama Specie Bank affairs, the lack of viable replacement leaders, and Premier Saito's consultations with Genro Prince Saionji.
subfiles.title: Extract from Periodic Report No. 76 (Internal Political Affairs)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 96 regarding the Kuroda scandal and predicted cabinet collapse.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Telegram No. 96 regarding the arrest of Vice-Minister of Finance Kuroda and predicting the fall of the Saito Cabinet and potential premiership of General Ugaki.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/233

subfiles.about: Reporting the arrest of Vice-Minister of Finance Kuroda and evaluating prospects for the Saito Cabinet's fall.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that the arrest of Vice-Minister of Finance Kuroda on bribery charges is likely to bring down the Saito Cabinet, which has failed in its mission of purifying politics. General Ugaki is identified as Saito's most probable successor, with Hirota and Hayashi likely remaining in any new cabinet.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 96 from Tokyo (Kuroda Scandal and Cabinet Crisis)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Periodic Report No. 77 on cabinet difficulties following the War Minister's resignation.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Periodic Report No. 77 (filed under 894.00 P.R./77) outlining the unfavorable position of the Saito Cabinet and its fright over Hayashi's resignation.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/234

subfiles.about: Extract from Periodic Report No. 77 analyzing the political instability of the Saito Cabinet and policy coordination by service ministries.
subfiles.summary: This report examines the precarious position of the Saito Cabinet following the scare of Hayashi's resignation and the unfilled Education portfolio. It reviews War Minister Hayashi's public endorsement of civilian diplomacy and non-interference in politics, contrasted with military demands for defense preparedness. Additionally, it surveys Navy support for the foreign office's China policy and preparations for the upcoming naval conference, including resistance to submarine abolition.
subfiles.title: Extract from Periodic Report No. 77 (Political Crisis and Defense Policies)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 814 commenting on the weakening of the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Despatch No. 814 (894.00/523) commenting on the failure and weakening of the Saito Cabinet through successive resignations.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/234 (Despatch 814)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 121 reporting the collapse of General Ugaki's candidacy for Prime Minister.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Telegram No. 121 reporting that General Ugaki's candidacy to succeed Saito has collapsed due to Army and Navy opposition.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/235

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Periodic Report No. 78 on the Kuroda scandal and premiership manoeuvring.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Periodic Report No. 78 regarding the position of the cabinet following the Kuroda scandal, prospective successors, and service ministry attitudes.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/236

subfiles.about: Extract from Periodic Report No. 78 covering the Kuroda scandal, potential premier candidates, party alignments, and service ministry shifts.
subfiles.summary: This detailed section recounts the arrest of Vice-Minister Kuroda and four Finance Ministry officials, threatening Takahashi's resignation and cabinet collapse. It examines prospective premiers including General Ugaki and Count Kiyoura, political party maneuvers by Seiyukai and Minseito, upcoming high-level Army reshuffles, and controversy surrounding Navy spokesman Rear Admiral Sakano's political remarks.
subfiles.title: Extract from Periodic Report No. 78 (Kuroda Scandal and Succession Maneuvering)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 831 on efforts to maintain the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Despatch No. 831 (894.00/526) discussing difficulties facing the Saito Cabinet and attempts to keep it in power.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/237

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 136 indicating the imminent en bloc resignation of the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Telegram No. 136 regarding the likelihood of the Saito Cabinet resigning en bloc or being reconstituted.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/238

subfiles.about: Reporting growing likelihood of the Saito Cabinet's en bloc resignation or reconstitution under Saito.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that indications are increasingly strong that the Saito Cabinet will be forced to resign en bloc shortly, though a reconstitution under Saito remains possible due to difficulties finding an acceptable successor.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 136 from Tokyo (Imminent Resignation of Saito Cabinet)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 141 announcing the en bloc resignation of the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Telegram No. 141 reporting the resignation en bloc of the Saito Cabinet on July 3, 1934.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/239

subfiles.about: Announcing that the Saito Cabinet resigned en bloc on July 3, 1934.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the Saito Cabinet resigned en bloc today, with expectations that several days will elapse before a new cabinet is formed.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 141 from Tokyo (Saito Cabinet Resigns En Bloc)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 144 reporting Admiral Okada's appointment to form a cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Telegram No. 144 regarding the Emperor charging Admiral Keisuke Okada with forming a new cabinet.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/240

subfiles.about: Reporting that the Emperor has commanded Admiral Keisuke Okada to form a new cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew cables that former Navy Minister Admiral Okada has been commanded by the Emperor to form a new cabinet, with individual appointments not yet announced.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 144 from Tokyo (Admiral Okada Charged to Form Cabinet)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Eugene Dooman's memorandum on the selection of Admiral Okada.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing a memorandum by Eugene H. Dooman of the Far Eastern Division analyzing the selection of Admiral Okada and reasons for the Saito Cabinet's fall.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/241

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 146 announcing key ministerial appointments in the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Telegram No. 146 listing ministerial retentions and appointments announced by Rengo.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/242

subfiles.about: Reporting Rengo's announcement of key ministerial appointments in the newly formed Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew transmits news service announcements confirming that Hirota, Hayashi, and Osumi will retain their posts as Ministers of Foreign Affairs, War, and Navy, while Vice-Minister Sadanobu Fujii becomes Finance Minister. He also cites Wilfrid Fleisher's 1932 interview with Admiral Okada.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 146 from Tokyo (Okada Cabinet Key Appointments)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 147 containing an appraisal of the Okada Cabinet by a prominent Japanese source.
subfiles.summary: A document file note indexing Telegram No. 147 providing a high-level confidential Japanese estimate of the new Okada Cabinet as a victory for moderates.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/243

subfiles.about: Transmitting a confidential evaluation of the Okada Cabinet from a well-placed Japanese informant as a victory for moderates.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the assessment of an influential Japanese insider who characterized the Okada Cabinet as a decisive triumph of moderate and liberal forces over chauvinist fanatics. The informant noted that the selection bodes well for U.S.-Japan relations and predicted Admiral Osumi would soon be succeeded by Admiral Nomura or Kobayashi rather than the hardline Suetsugu. Grew confirms that the appointments reflect a broad moderate resurgence.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 147 from Tokyo (Confidential Evaluation of Okada Cabinet)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Telegram No. 153 on the formal installation of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Telegram No. 153 regarding the completion and formal installation of the Okada Cabinet on July 8.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/244

subfiles.about: Reporting the completion and formal imperial installation of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Admiral Okada has completed his cabinet, which was formally received and installed by the Emperor on July 8.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 153 from Tokyo (Installation of Okada Cabinet)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Periodic Report No. 79 on cabinet resignation prospects and the Army's posture.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Tokyo Periodic Report No. 79 on the probability of cabinet resignation and the attitude of the Army.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/245

subfiles.about: Extract from Periodic Report No. 79 discussing public clamor over the Kuroda scandal and military pressure during the final days of the Saito Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: This periodic report extract details the political crisis surrounding the Justice Ministry's investigation into Vice-Minister Kuroda and potential involvement of higher officials. It analyzes Finance Minister Takahashi's conditional resignation, discussions among senior ministers leading to the decision to resign en bloc, and War Minister Hayashi's efforts to balance military defense demands while keeping the army out of overt politics.
subfiles.title: Extract from Periodic Report No. 79 (Imminent Fall of Saito Ministry)

subfiles.about: Military Intelligence service biography of Admiral Keisuke Okada detailing his naval career and political characteristics.
subfiles.summary: Intelligence Report No. 105 provides an extensive service record of Admiral Keisuke Okada from his birth in Fukui in 1868, service on the Naniwa, torpedo expertise, command of the Combined Fleet, through two tenures as Navy Minister. Characterized as straightforward, unassuming, and a consummate negotiator, he is judged well-suited to navigate party politics and restrain radical militarism.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report No. 105 (Admiral Keisuke Okada - Prime Minister)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 896 providing a full account of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: A document file note cross-referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 896 detailing the formation, ministerial biographies, and political standing of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.002/247

subfiles.about: Comprehensive diplomatic despatch analyzing the formation, ministerial roster, party alignments, policies, and background of the Okada Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew submits an exhaustive report on the Okada Cabinet installed on July 8, 1934. He analyzes the cabinet's 'national' composition—combining military officers, career bureaucrats, Minseito members, and expelled Seiyukai dissidents led by Tokonami—and notes the unusual absence of peers. The report reviews initial statements by Foreign Minister Hirota, Finance Minister Fujii, and Justice Minister Obara, alongside Navy Minister Osumi's demand for naval parity, concluding with human-interest anecdotes detailing Okada's modest personal finances.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 896 from Tokyo (The Okada Cabinet)

subfiles.about: Departmental and War Department routing sheets for a G-2 report on the Okada Cabinet and naval policy.
subfiles.summary: A cover memorandum from Dr. Stanley K. Hornbeck to Under Secretary Phillips calling attention to a G-2 Military Intelligence Division study titled 'Japan: The New Okada Cabinet and Japan's Naval Program,' accompanied by standard War Department routing slips.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Routing Slip on G-2 Naval Program Report
